info.title: Smart Taxi API
info.description:
Backend API for **Smart Taxi**, a ride-hailing (Uber-like) application.

## Overview
Currently exposes customer authentication, notifications, ride-ordering, and driver authentication endpoints. More modules (driver vehicles, wallets, etc.) will be added here as they ship.

## Authentication
Successful signup / login returns:
- `accessToken` — short-lived JWT (default **15m**). Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on protected routes.
- `refreshToken` — opaque token stored hashed in the DB (default **30 days**). Used to obtain a new access token without re-logging in.

JWT payload claims: `sub` (owner id), `ownerType` (`customer` | `driver`), `accountTypeId` (`1` customer, `2` manager).

## Common response envelope
**Success**
```json
{ "success": true, "message": "...", "data": { } }
```

**Error**
```json
{ "success": false, "message": "...", "errors": { "field": "reason" } }
```
`errors` is only present for validation (422) and conflict (409) responses.

BearerAuth.description: JWT access token from signup/login. Header: `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`

photo_url.description: Absolute or relative URL to the profile photo

phone_number.description: Unique phone number used as the login identifier

language.description: App language — notifications are sent in it. Set via PUT /api/customer/profile/language

is_guest.description: Created by a manager for a phone order (no password). Signing up in the app with the same phone claims it — same id, ride history kept.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token (hex). Store securely on the client.

refreshTokenExpiresAt.description: ISO-8601 expiry of the refresh token

AccountBlockInfo.description: Temporary block set by a manager. While `is_blocked`: a driver gets no offers and cannot accept; a customer cannot order. Login still works.

cancel_strikes.description: Cancels after accept since the last block / dismiss (`strikes_since`)

strikes_since.description: Last block / dismiss; null = since the account was created

example.password: password must contain at least one number

first_name.description: Letters only (any language). Spaces, hyphens and apostrophes allowed between words. No digits.

phone_number.description: Must be a **string** (so leading zeros are kept). Digits only; optional leading `+`. 8–15 digits. Arabic/Persian digits are normalized. Unique.

email.description: Optional. Max 150 chars. Unique when provided.

password.description: 8–64 chars, no spaces, at least one letter and one number

device_info.description: Optional. Stored with the refresh token for session tracking. Falls back to User-Agent if omitted.

fcm_token.description: Optional Firebase Cloud Messaging device token. Stored in `device_tokens` for push notifications.

platform.description: Optional. Required context for FCM; defaults to `android` when `fcm_token` is sent.

phone_number.description: Same phone validation rules as signup

password.description: Presence check only (no strength rules) so existing accounts are not locked out

device_info.description: Optional. Stored with the refresh token. Falls back to User-Agent if omitted.

platform.description: Optional. Defaults to `android` when `fcm_token` is sent.

refresh_token.description: Required unless `all_devices` is true. Opaque refresh token from signup/login.

all_devices.description: When true, revokes every active refresh token for this customer

notification_type.description: App-defined type key used by the client for routing/UI

unread_count.description: Total unread notifications for this customer (badge)

Ride.description: Customer-facing ride/order. Internal commission split fields are not exposed here.

driver_id.description: Set once a driver accepts the ride

order_source.description: Static order channel. Customer app flow always stores `app` (do not send it). `whatsapp` / `call` for manager-created orders.

distance_km.description: Estimated straight-line (Haversine) distance at order time

actual_distance_km.description: Distance the driver reported at finish (null until completed)

estimated_duration_min.description: Heuristic ETA based on an average city speed

waiting_fee.description: Waiting-at-pickup fee (final once the trip started; 0 if none). Included in price at finish.

pause_fee_total.description: Fees of closed pauses during the trip (final amounts). Included in price at finish.

pauses.description: Each pause of the trip (single-ride detail endpoints only)

arrived_at.description: When the driver tapped arrived (waiting timer start)

price.description: Estimated price until the ride is completed; after finish = final price (base_fare + actual_distance_km × price_per_km + stops_fee_total)

estimated_price.description: Price quoted at order time (never changes)

final_price.description: Amount due, set once the ride is completed (= price); null before that

payment_status.description: Becomes `paid` when the driver confirms the customer paid (or a manager marks it paid). completed + unpaid = customer still has to pay the driver

has_route.description: The driver uploaded the driven GPS route for this ride

route_distance_km.description: Length of the uploaded route (sum of point-to-point distances); null if no route

route.description: Driven GPS path in time order, or null if none was uploaded. Only on the single-ride detail endpoints (never in lists). With ?simplify=true the path is thinned (~10 m tolerance).

cancelled_by.description: Who cancelled the ride (null unless cancelled)

stops.description: Only included on the single-ride detail endpoint

vehicle_type_id.description: Must reference an active row in vehicle_types

stops.description: Optional intermediate stops (max 5). Each adds the current stop fee.

language.description: App language — notifications are sent in it. Set via PUT /api/driver/language

fcm_token.description: Optional Firebase Cloud Messaging device token. Stored for push notifications. (Not collected on driver signup.)

platform.description: Optional. Defaults to `android` when `fcm_token` is sent.

waiting_fee.description: Waiting-at-pickup fee (final once the trip started; 0 if none). Included in price at finish.

content.example:
# Privacy Policy

**Effective date and last updated:** September 30, 2026

## 1. Who we are
...

url.description: Same text as a web page (for a web view or "open in browser")

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 with timezone; returned normalized to UTC (…Z)

RideWaiting.description: Waiting at pickup (driver tapped arrived → started trip). null if the driver never tapped arrived. While is_running, elapsed_seconds is measured by the server at response time — count up from it locally.

elapsed_seconds.description: Live (at response time) while running; final after start; null if cancelled while waiting

billable_minutes.description: Every started minute after the free minutes

fee.description: Fee so far while running; final after start

RidePause.description: Pauses during the trip (always present). current = the running pause (null if not paused); its elapsed_seconds is measured by the server at response time — count up from it locally. count / total_seconds / total_fee cover closed pauses only.

fee.description: Fee of this pause so far

RidePayment.description: Payment settlement returned by driver confirm-payment (`data.payment`) and admin mark-paid (`data`). The driver keeps the cash (`driver_share`); `manager_share` is deducted from the driver wallet.

wallet_transaction_id.description: null when the commission is 0 (no wallet movement)

SocketCustomerRideStatus.description: Socket event `customer:ride_status` (server → customer). Also sent as `driver:ride_status` to the driver. Extra fields depend on status: `completed` adds final_price / estimated_price / actual_distance_km / payment_status (always `unpaid` at finish); `cancelled` adds cancellation_reason / cancelled_by.

SocketCustomerRidePaid.description: Socket event `customer:ride_paid` (server → customer). Sent live when the driver confirms payment or a manager marks the order paid, and **replayed on every customer socket connect** for the latest completed ride if it was paid within the last 24 h. Also replayed after `customer:track_ride` on a paid ride. Idempotent — match by `ride_id`.

SocketCustomerActiveRide.description: Socket event `customer:active_ride` (server → customer), sent on every customer connect and after `customer:track_ride`. `ride` is, in order: the live trip (accepted / arrived / in_progress), else the latest **completed ride with payment_status = unpaid** (show "pay the driver"), else `null`. A paid ride is never returned here on connect — its state comes via the `customer:ride_paid` replay.

driver.description: id, first_name, last_name, photo_url, phone_number, rating

location.description: Last driver GPS; always null for a completed ride

password.description: New password — same strength rules as signup (letters + numbers, no spaces)

logout_devices.description:
Sign the user out on every device (revokes all refresh tokens), so the old password's
sessions end and they must log in with the new one. Send `false` to keep existing sessions.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed (e.g. non-customer token)

ValidationError.description: One or more fields failed validation

errors.password: password must be between 8 and 64 characters

get.summary: Health check
get.description: Returns a simple status payload confirming the service is running.

get.summary: List all customers (paginated)
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns customers with `account_type_id = 1` (excludes managers),
newest first.

Each customer includes a live **`live_status`** + `active_ride_id`:
`idle` | `searching` (waiting for a driver) | `driver_on_the_way` |
`driver_arrived` | `in_progress`. Realtime updates: socket `manager:customer_status`.

Each customer includes a **paginated** `orders` list (newest first) plus
`orders_count` / `orders_pagination`. Nested page size is controlled by
`orders_page` / `orders_limit` (same values applied to every customer on
the page — loaded in one batched SQL query for performance).

parameters.name: orders_limit
parameters.description: Orders per customer on this response

post.summary: Create a customer account
post.description:
Manager-only. Creates a customer (`account_type_id = 1`) with a bcrypt-hashed
password. Does **not** issue tokens — the customer signs in later via
`POST /api/customer/auth/login`.

**Validation rules** (same as customer signup)
| Field | Rules |
|-------|-------|
| `first_name` / `last_name` | Required, 2–100 chars, letters only |
| `phone_number` | Required string, 8–15 digits, unique |
| `email` | Optional, valid email, unique when provided |
| `password` | Required, 8–64 chars, ≥1 letter and ≥1 number |
| `address` | Optional, max 255 chars |

409.description: Phone or email already registered

put.description:
Manager-only. Partial update — send any of `first_name`, `last_name`,
`phone_number`, `email`, `address`, `password`.
Only customers (`account_type_id = 1`) can be updated.

409.description: Phone or email already registered

put.description:
Sets a new password for the customer — no old password needed. Manager accounts can't
be changed here (`404`). By default the customer is signed out on all devices.
The manager tells the customer the new password; it's never returned or sent by the API.

Sets a new password for the driver — no old password needed. By default the driver is
signed out on all devices. The manager tells the driver the new password; it's never
returned or sent by the API.

get.summary: List all drivers (paginated)
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns all drivers with status name, newest first.

`status` = **account** status (pending / active / suspended / rejected).
`live_status` = **what the driver is doing now**:
`offline` | `free` | `on_the_way` (heading to pickup) | `arrived` | `in_progress`,
plus `is_online` and `active_ride_id`. A driver on a trip keeps the trip status
even if their app disconnects. Realtime updates: socket `manager:driver_status`.

Each driver includes:
- fines (غرامات): `fines`, `fines_count`, `fines_total`
- wallet history: `wallet_transactions`, `wallet_transactions_count`
- vehicle: brand, model, color, plate, type, photo (or null)
- **paginated** `orders` (newest first) plus `orders_count` /
  `orders_pagination` — controlled by `orders_page` / `orders_limit`
  (same values for every driver on the page; one batched SQL query)

parameters.name: orders_limit
parameters.description: Orders per driver on this response

put.description:
Manager-only. Sets `drivers.status_id`.

| ID | Name | Meaning |
|----|------|---------|
| 1 | pending | Waiting for approval |
| 2 | active | Can go online and accept rides |
| 3 | suspended | Temporarily blocked |
| 4 | rejected | Application rejected |

When status is not `active`, the driver is forced offline (`is_online = false`).

post.summary: Issue a fine (غرامة) on a driver
post.description:
Manager-only. Creates a fine with a **reason** and **amount**.

- Stores the fine in `driver_warnings`
- If `amount > 0`, deducts from the driver's wallet and records a wallet `penalty` transaction
- Sends an in-app notification to the driver

reason.example: Cancelled ride after pickup without reason

example.reason: Cancelled ride after pickup without reason

fine.reason: Cancelled ride after pickup without reason

fines.reason: Cancelled ride after pickup without reason

post.summary: Add amount to a driver's wallet
post.description:
Manager-only. Credits (top-up) the driver's `wallet_balance` and records a
`topup` wallet transaction. Notifies the driver.

get.summary: Get driver wallet history (paginated)
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns the driver's current `wallet_balance` and paginated
transactions from `driver_wallet_transactions` (no DB schema change needed).

Types: `topup`, `commission_deduction`, `penalty`, `compensation`, `reward`.

post.summary: Add a reward to a driver's wallet
post.description:
Manager-only. Credits the driver's `wallet_balance` and records a
`reward` wallet transaction (مكافأة). Notifies the driver.
Distinct from wallet top-up (`topup`).

get.summary: List all orders / rides (paginated)
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns all ride orders newest-first (`requested_at` DESC).

Optional inclusive date range filter on `requested_at`:
- `from_date` — start of day (YYYY-MM-DD)
- `to_date` — end of day (YYYY-MM-DD)

post.summary: Create an order for a phone / WhatsApp caller
post.description:
Manager-only. Customer is **either** `customer_id` (picked from lookup) **or**
`customer` with `phone_number` — an existing customer with that phone is used, otherwise
a guest account is created (then `first_name` + `last_name` are required). When that
person later signs up in the app with the same phone, the guest becomes their account
and keeps the ride history.

Dispatch:
- without `driver_id` the order is offered to nearby matching drivers exactly like an
  app order (`dispatch.mode = broadcast`)
- with `driver_id` the driver is validated first (active, has a car of the chosen
  vehicle type, not on a ride) and the order is assigned straight away
  (`dispatch.mode = assigned`). The driver app gets `driver:active_ride` with
  `assigned_by_manager: true` plus a push; the customer gets the normal accepted events.
  If the driver took another ride in the same moment, the order falls back to broadcast
  and `dispatch.assign_error` explains why.

Price is calculated on the server (same rules as the app). `order_source` defaults to `call`.

409 when the customer already has an active ride (`errors.active_ride_id`), when the
same customer is being submitted twice at once, or when the phone belongs to a manager
or a deleted account.

driver_id.description: Assign directly to this driver instead of broadcasting

created.description: A guest account was created by this request

409.description: Active ride exists / duplicate submit / phone not usable / driver busy or inactive

422.description: Invalid body / names missing for a new caller / driver vehicle type mismatch

get.summary: Get any order with its stops and driven route
get.description:
Full `AdminOrder` for one ride (any customer / driver), plus `stops` and `route`.

`route` is the GPS path the driver uploaded after the trip
(`[{ lat, lng, recorded_at }]` in time order), or `null` if none was uploaded —
the same points `GET /api/customer/rides/{id}` returns to the ride's customer.
Compare `route_distance_km` (from the points) with `actual_distance_km`
(what the driver reported at finish) to spot fare disputes.

`?simplify=true` drops near-collinear points (~10 m tolerance) for small maps.

post.summary: Mark a completed order as paid (driver never tapped "Payment received")
post.description:
Manager-only fallback for a finished ride that is still `payment_status = unpaid`.
Runs exactly the same settlement as the driver's
`POST /api/driver/rides/{id}/confirm-payment`:
- ride `payment_status` → `paid`, `paid_at` set, `payment_confirmed_by` → `manager`
- the commission (`manager_share`) is deducted from the driver's wallet as a
  `commission_deduction` transaction (`created_by_user_id` = this manager)
- emits the same `customer:ride_paid` (so the customer app closes its
  "pay the driver" dialog), `driver:ride_paid`, `manager:ride_paid`
- push notification to the customer and the driver

200.description: Order marked paid and money split

409.description: Order is not completed, or already paid

get.summary: List vehicle types
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns all car classes (economy, comfort, …), active and inactive,
ordered by `id`. Optional `is_active` filter.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: If set, only return active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) types

post.summary: Create a vehicle type
post.description:
Manager-only. Creates a car class (e.g. `comfort`, `VIP`, `economy`).
Name must be unique. New types are active by default (`is_active: true`).

409.description: Name already taken

put.description:
Manager-only. Partial update — send any of `name`, `description`, `is_active`.
Use `is_active: true` to re-activate a soft-deleted type.

409.description: Name already taken

delete.description:
Manager-only. Soft-delete — sets `is_active = false` so existing rides /
driver vehicles keep their FK. Inactive types cannot be chosen for new
rides or driver signup. Re-activate with PUT `is_active: true`.

409.description: Already inactive

get.summary: List pricing tiers
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns saved distance pricing bands (all vehicle types),
ordered by vehicle type then `min_distance_km`.
Optional filters: `vehicle_type_id`, `is_active`.

parameters.name: vehicle_type_id
parameters.description: Only tiers for this vehicle type

post.summary: Create a distance pricing tier
post.description:
Manager-only. Adds a distance band for a vehicle type, e.g. comfort:
- 0–5 km → `price_per_km` 500
- 5–8 km → `price_per_km` 800

`max_distance_km` may be `null` for an open-ended upper band (e.g. 8+ km).
Touching endpoints are allowed (`0–5` then `5–8`); interior overlaps return 409.

Quote formula: `base_fare + distance_km * price_per_km + stops_fee`.

409.description: Distance range overlaps another active tier

put.description:
Manager-only. Partial update of distance band / rates / active flag.
Re-activate with `is_active: true`.

404.description: Pricing tier or vehicle type not found

409.description: Distance range overlaps another active tier

delete.description:
Manager-only. Soft-delete (`is_active = false`). Inactive tiers are not
used for new ride quotes. Re-activate with PUT `is_active: true`.

409.description: Already inactive

get.summary: Get current commission percentage
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns the platform / manager commission `%` taken from
each order price when a ride is created.

Example: `rate_percentage = 10` and order price `1000` →
manager gets `100`, driver gets `900`.

put.description:
Manager-only. Sets the flat platform / manager commission `%` for **new** orders.
Inserts a history row (old rates stay for past rides). Cache is invalidated
immediately so the next order uses the new rate.

**Used only when no commission tiers exist** — see `PUT /api/admin/commission-tiers`
(commission % by trip distance).

Allowed range: `0` – `100`.

rate_percentage.description: Percent of order price taken by manager / platform

get.summary: Get the waiting fee at pickup
get.description:
Manager-only. When the driver taps "arrived" a timer starts; it stops when the driver
starts the trip. The first `free_minutes` are free, then every **started** minute costs
`price_per_minute` (e.g. free 3, price 500, waited 5 min 10 s → 3 billable minutes → 1500).
The fee is added to the final price at finish (commission applies to the total).

`price_per_minute = 0` (default until set) means waiting is free.

put.summary: Set the waiting fee at pickup
put.description:
Manager-only. Applies to drivers who tap "arrived" **after** this call — a ride already
waiting keeps the rules locked at its arrival. Inserts a history row; cache is cleared
immediately. Omit `free_minutes` to keep the current value (default 3).

get.summary: Get the pause fee (stop during the trip)
get.description:
Manager-only. During a trip the driver can tap **pause** (customer stops e.g. for a coffee)
and **resume**. Each pause costs `base_fee`, which covers the first `included_minutes`;
after that every **started** minute costs `price_per_minute`.
Example: base 2000 / 3 min / 500 → paused 5 min 20 s → 2000 + 3 × 500 = 3500.
Several pauses in one trip are charged separately. The total is added to the final price
(commission applies to it).

All `0` (default until set) means pausing is free.

put.summary: Set the pause fee (stop during the trip)
put.description:
Manager-only. Partial update — send any of the fields; omitted ones keep their current
value. Applies to pauses started **after** this call (a running pause keeps its rules).
Inserts a history row; cache is cleared immediately.

post.summary: Send notification to a customer or driver
post.description:
Manager-only. Creates an in-app notification and pushes via Firebase FCM
to the recipient's registered device tokens (`fcm_token` from login/signup).

`notification_type` is always stored as `manager_message`.

**Language:** the recipient gets the text in their saved app language (`ar` / `en`).
Send `title_ar` / `body_ar` and `title_en` / `body_en` to provide both versions;
a missing version falls back to `title` / `body`. `title` / `body` can be omitted
only when both language versions are sent. The response shows the text actually sent.

body_ar.example: يرجى تحديث التطبيق إلى آخر إصدار.

body_en.example: Please update the app to the latest version.

body.example: Please update the app to the latest version.

bilingual.summary: Both languages — recipient gets their own

value.body_ar: يرجى تحديث التطبيق إلى آخر إصدار.
value.body_en: Please update the app to the latest version.

toDriver.summary: Notify a driver (same text for any language)

value.title: System update
value.body: Please update the app to the latest version.

value.title: Promo
value.body: Enjoy 10% off your next ride this week.

201.description: Notification created and FCM push attempted

data.title: تحديث النظام
data.body: يرجى تحديث التطبيق إلى آخر إصدار.

post.summary: Send a notification to all customers, all drivers, or everyone
post.description:
Manager-only. One call notifies a whole audience:
- `POST /api/admin/notifications/broadcast/customers`: every customer account (managers excluded)
- `POST /api/admin/notifications/broadcast/drivers`: every driver except rejected applications
- `POST /api/admin/notifications/broadcast/all`: both of the above

Each recipient gets an in-app notification (`notification_type = manager_broadcast`,
visible in their notifications list) and a Firebase push on their registered devices.

**Language:** each recipient gets the text in their saved app language (`ar` / `en`).
Send `title_ar` / `body_ar` and `title_en` / `body_en`; a missing version falls back to
`title` / `body`, which can be omitted only when both language versions are sent.

In-app rows are saved before the response; pushes are sent in the background right after.
`data.recipients` counts recipients per language (users without a device still get the
in-app notification). Push data includes `notification_type`, `language`, `sent_by`, `audience`.

get.summary: List all complaints (paginated)
get.description:
Manager-only. Returns all complaints from customers and drivers,
newest first. Optional filter by `status`.

complaints.subject: Customer no-show
complaints.message: Customer was not at the pickup point after waiting 10 minutes.

Manager-only. Sets complaint status to one of:
`open`, `in_review`, `resolved`, `closed`.

data.subject: Driver was rude
data.message: The driver spoke aggressively during the trip.

get.summary: Drivers / customers who cancelled too many accepted rides
get.description:
Manager-only. A strike is added when:
- a driver cancels a ride he accepted (accepted / arrived / in_progress), or
- a customer cancels after a driver accepted.

Strikes count since the last block or dismiss (no time window). Nobody is blocked
automatically: from 3 strikes the account appears here (`status=flagged`) and
`manager:cancel_alert` is emitted to the managers socket room.

`status=blocked` lists blocks still running. `flagged_count` is for the menu badge.

get.summary: Strike detail for one driver or customer
get.description:
Manager-only. Current strike / block state, the cancelled rides that make up the
current strikes (newest first, max 50), and the block history (max 20).
Works for any driver / customer, flagged or not.

unblocked_at.description: Set when a manager ended the block early

post.summary: Block a driver or customer from rides for N hours
post.description:
Manager-only. Default 24 hours, max 720 (30 days). Blocking again replaces the running
block (new end time). Strikes reset to 0.

Effect until `blocked_until`:
- driver: gets no ride offers, accept returns 403, cannot be assigned by a manager.
  A ride already in progress can still be finished.
- customer: creating an order in the app returns 403.

Login still works; profiles show `block`. The user gets a push notification.

post.summary: End a block early
post.description: Manager-only. The user gets a push notification. Strikes stay at 0.

409.description: This account is not blocked

post.summary: Reviewed — do not block, start counting again
post.description: Manager-only. Strikes go back to 0 and the account leaves the flagged list.

post.summary: Manager / admin login
post.description:
Login for managers (`account_type_id = 2` in `customers`).
Regular customer accounts cannot use this endpoint.

401.description: Invalid credentials or not a manager

get.summary: Drivers who asked to delete their account
get.description:
Manager-only. Newest first. Defaults to `status=pending`; `status=all` lists everything.
Each item has the driver's current `wallet_balance` (settle it before approving if needed)
and `pending_count` is the badge number.

Live updates: the socket event `manager:driver_deletion_request` `{ request, driver?, updated_at }`
fires when a request is created, cancelled, approved or rejected.

After approval the driver shows as "Deleted Driver" (personal data is erased).

post.summary: Approve — delete the driver account now
post.description:
Manager-only. Erases the driver's personal data (name, phone, photo, address, car plate
and photo), sets status `deleted`, signs out every device and disconnects the live socket.
Rides, wallet transactions and fines stay for accounting. The wallet balance is not
changed — it is returned so the dashboard can show it.

Refused (**409**) while the driver is on a trip or when the request is no longer pending.

409.description: Driver is on a trip or the request is not pending

post.summary: Reject — keep the driver account
post.description:
Manager-only. The driver gets a notification (push + in-app) with the optional `note`
and can see it in `GET /api/driver/account/deletion-request`. The driver may ask again later.

note.example: Please settle your wallet balance first

409.description: The request is not pending

get.summary: Find a caller by phone while typing
get.description:
Manager-only. Prefix search on the phone number (at least 4 digits), max 10 results,
exact match first. Deleted accounts and managers are excluded.

When the full phone matches a customer, `exact` also carries what the form needs for a
one-click order: `active_ride` (if not null, a new order returns 409), `saved_addresses`
and `recent_places` (last distinct pickup / dropoff points). `exact` is null otherwise —
the dashboard then asks for first + last name and a guest account is created on submit.

Debounce ~300 ms and cancel the previous request (AbortController).

422.description: phone missing or shorter than 4 digits

post.summary: Prices per vehicle type + free drivers for the chosen pins
post.description:
Manager-only. One call once pickup and dropoff are set (repeat when a pin or the
stops change). Returns the estimated price of every active vehicle type (stops included),
waiting / pause fee rules, and `available_drivers`: active drivers with a car and no
active ride — online first, nearest to pickup first, max 30. Filter them by the
selected `vehicle_type_id` on the client (no new request).

post.summary: Give a waiting order to a specific driver
post.description:
Manager-only. Works for any order still `requested` (app or dashboard) — e.g. nobody
accepted the broadcast. Same checks and events as `driver_id` on create. The open offer
cards are removed from the other drivers. 409 if the order is no longer waiting.

409.description: Order not waiting / driver busy or inactive

422.description: Driver vehicle type does not match

post.summary: Cancel an order that has not started
post.description:
Manager-only. Any order in `requested`, `accepted` or `arrived` (any source).
`cancelled_by = manager`. Offer cards are removed, the customer and the assigned
driver get `*:ride_status` (cancelled) and a push.

409.description: Trip already started or ended

get.summary: Pricing page — every vehicle type with its distance tiers + commission tiers
get.description:
Manager-only. One call for the whole pricing screen.

The final fare is `distance_km × price_per_km` (+ `base_fare`, usually 0) of the tier
whose range contains the distance (e.g. 2.5 km in "2.4–2.8 at 1200" → 2.5 × 1200 = 3000),
plus stops / waiting / pause fees. The commission % comes from the commission tier that
contains the same distance.

get.summary: Fare calculator — what a trip of N km costs with the current rules
get.description:
Manager-only. Uses the live rules (same code as finishing a trip): distance tier,
`distance_fare`, `price`, commission %, manager / driver split. Waiting, pause and
stop fees are not included.

`can_order = false` when no tier covers the distance (customers can't order it;
finishing such a trip uses the first / last tier).

get.summary: Distance tiers of one vehicle type (price per km)

put.summary: Save (replace) all distance tiers of one vehicle type
put.description:
Manager-only. Sends the **whole table** for the vehicle type; it replaces the current
tiers atomically (old tiers are kept inactive as history). Applies immediately to new
quotes and to trips finished from now on.

Rules:
- 1–50 tiers, any order (sorted by `min_distance_km` on save), distances in **km**
  (up to 3 decimals = meters, e.g. `0.51`, `9.801`).
- Ranges must not overlap. Touching (`0–0.5`, `0.5–2.5`) and small gaps
  (`0–0.5`, `0.51–2.5`) are both fine; a distance in a gap uses the tier below it,
  on a shared boundary the lower tier wins.
- Only the last tier may have `max_distance_km: null` (= and above).
- Customers can't order a distance above the last tier's max (or below the first min).

422.description: Validation failed — errors keyed `tiers[i].field` (i = index in your request)

get.summary: Commission % by trip distance
get.description:
Manager-only. The commission % of a trip comes from the tier containing its distance
(estimated distance at order time, real distance at finish). When `tiers` is empty,
the flat `fallback_rate_percentage` (`PUT /api/admin/commission`) applies.

put.description:
Manager-only. Replaces the whole list atomically (old list kept inactive as history).
Same range rules as pricing tiers; the first tier must start at 0 and a distance above
the last tier uses the last tier. Send `tiers: []` to go back to the flat rate.

post.summary: Register a new customer account
post.description:
Creates a customer account (`account_type_id = 1`), hashes the password with bcrypt,
and immediately issues an access JWT + refresh token so the client can stay logged in.

**Validation rules**
| Field | Rules |
|-------|-------|
| `first_name` / `last_name` | Required, 2–100 chars, letters only (any language). Spaces, hyphens, apostrophes allowed between words. No digits. |
| `phone_number` | Required **string**, 8–15 digits, optional leading `+`. Arabic/Persian digits normalized. Unique. |
| `email` | Optional, valid email, max 150 chars. Unique when provided. |
| `password` | Required, 8–64 chars, no spaces, ≥1 letter and ≥1 number. |
| `address` | Optional, max 255 chars. |
| `device_info` | Optional, max 255 chars. Stored with the refresh token; falls back to `User-Agent`. |
| `fcm_token` | Optional, max 500 chars. Firebase device token → `device_tokens`. |
| `platform` | Optional `ios` \| `android` (defaults to `android` if token sent). |

**Side effects**
- Inserts a row into `customers`
- Inserts a hashed refresh token into `auth_refresh_tokens`
- Upserts `device_tokens` when `fcm_token` is provided

post.summary: Log in an existing customer
post.description:
Authenticates a customer by phone number + password and issues a new access JWT + refresh token.

**Rules**
- Only accounts with `account_type_id = 1` (customer) can use this endpoint
- Wrong phone, wrong password, or non-customer account all return the **same** `401` message
  (`Invalid phone number or password`) to avoid account enumeration
- Password strength is **not** re-checked on login (presence only)

**Validation rules**
| Field | Rules |
|-------|-------|
| `phone_number` | Required string, 8–15 digits, optional leading `+` |
| `password` | Required string, max 64 chars |
| `device_info` | Optional, max 255 chars; falls back to `User-Agent` |
| `fcm_token` | Optional Firebase device token → upserted into `device_tokens` |
| `platform` | Optional `ios` \| `android` (default `android`) |

**Side effects**
- Inserts a new hashed refresh token into `auth_refresh_tokens` (previous sessions stay valid until expiry / logout)
- Upserts `device_tokens` when `fcm_token` is provided

post.summary: Log out the current customer session
post.description:
Soft-revokes refresh token(s) by setting `revoked_at` in `auth_refresh_tokens`.
The access JWT remains valid until it expires (short-lived by design).

**Modes**
| Body | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `{ "refresh_token": "..." }` | Revoke this device session only |
| `{ "all_devices": true }` | Revoke **all** active sessions for this customer |

Requires a valid customer access token. The refresh token must belong to the same customer.

401.description: Missing/invalid access token, or refresh token invalid/already revoked

post.summary: Delete an account with phone + password (public web page)
post.description:
No token needed — used by the public page `GET /delete-account`
(the "delete account" URL for Google Play). Same effect as `DELETE /api/customer/profile`:
personal data erased, all devices signed out, past rides kept anonymously.

- Wrong phone or wrong password → the same **401** (does not reveal who has an account).
- Limited to 5 attempts per phone and 20 per IP every 15 minutes (**429**).

409.description: The customer has an active ride

get.description:
Returns notifications where `recipient_type = customer` and `recipient_id` matches
the authenticated user, newest first.

Notifications are kept for **1 month** — older ones are deleted automatically
(hourly job) and never returned.

**Query params**
| Param | Default | Rules |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `page` | `1` | Integer ≥ 1 |
| `limit` | `20` | Integer 1–100 |
| `unread_only` | `false` | Boolean — when true, only unread rows |

Also returns `unread_count` for the badge (always the total unread for this user,
independent of the current filter/page).

get.summary: Get my profile
get.description: Customer-only. Returns the authenticated customer's own information.

put.description:
Customer-only. **Partial update** — send only the fields you want to change.

Editable: `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone_number`, `email`, `address`, `photo`.

- Send **JSON** for text fields only, or **multipart/form-data** to also upload `photo`
  (JPEG / PNG / WebP, max 5 MB). The old photo is replaced.
- `phone_number` is the login identifier — after changing it, log in with the new number.
- Send `email: ""` or `address: ""` to clear them.
- Password is **not** changed here → use `PUT /api/customer/profile/password`.

delete.description:
Customer-only. Permanently deletes the account, confirmed with the password.

- Refused (**409**) while a ride is requested / accepted / arrived / in progress —
  cancel or finish it first.
- Personal data is erased: name becomes "Deleted User"; phone, email, address, photo,
  saved addresses, notifications and push tokens are removed.
- Every device is signed out immediately (tokens stop working, sockets are disconnected).
- The phone number can be used to register a **new** account right away.
- Past rides and complaints are kept anonymously for the driver's and company's records.

After **200**: clear the stored tokens and go to the login / welcome screen.

409.description: The customer has an active ride

Customer-only. Requires the current password.

On success **all devices are signed out** and new tokens are returned for
this device — replace the stored `accessToken` / `refreshToken` (and reconnect the socket).

Customer-only. Saves the app language (`ar` or `en`). Every push and in-app
notification is sent to this customer in that language (new users default to `ar`).
Call it after login and whenever the user switches language in the app.

422.description: language must be one of ar, en

post.summary: Submit start/end lat/lng (order flow step 1)
post.description:
First step of the order flow. Client sends **pickup** and **dropoff**
coordinates (from the map). Server validates them and returns the same
points plus Haversine `distance_km` / ETA, and an **estimated** price
for every active vehicle type using the manager's pricing tiers:
`estimated_price = base_fare + (distance_km × price_per_km)`.

**These prices are not final** — they use straight-line distance. The
final fare may change if the driver takes a different route.

Optional `pickup_address` / `dropoff_address` are echoed back unchanged.
Does **not** create a ride — next call `POST /choose-vehicle`.

200.description: Locations accepted with per-vehicle-type estimated prices

data.price_note: Price is an estimate based on straight-line distance. Final fare may change if the driver takes a different route.

post.summary: Choose vehicle type and request the ride (order flow step 2)
post.description:
Second step of the order flow. Customer picks a `vehicle_type_id` from
step 1 (`vehicle_types`) and sends the same pickup/dropoff coordinates.

Creates a ride with **`status_id = 1` (`requested`)**.

Eligible drivers are then offered the ride on socket (`driver:order_offer` cards + optional FCM) when:
1. They are **not** on an active order (accepted / arrived / in_progress)
2. Pickup is within their `search_radius_km`
3. Their registered vehicle type matches `vehicle_type_id`
(also: active, online, has GPS — live socket location preferred)

Response includes `notified_drivers_count` and `notify_stats` so you can
see how many drivers matched each filter.

201.description: Vehicle chosen; ride requested with estimated price

example.message: Vehicle selected and ride requested. Shown price is an estimate and may change if the driver takes a different route.

data.price_note: Price is an estimate based on straight-line distance. Final fare may change if the driver takes a different route.

422.description: Validation failed or no pricing tier for this distance/type

get.summary: List the authenticated customer's ride orders
get.description:
Paginated, newest-first list of the customer's rides. Filter by `status_id` to
show e.g. only active or only completed orders. Uses the `idx_customer_status`
composite index for fast filtered lookups.

Status IDs: 1=requested, 2=accepted, 3=arrived, 4=in_progress, 5=completed, 6=cancelled
(full reference: `docs/ride_statuses.md`).

get.summary: Get a single ride order (including its current status)
get.description:
Returns full ride details, including its current `status` and, if any, its
stops. Looked up by primary key — only rides belonging to the authenticated
customer are returned (others → `404`, never leaked as `403`).

Payment check (fallback on app resume / reconnect): a ride with
`status = completed` and `payment_status = unpaid` still needs to be paid —
amount due is `final_price`. Once `payment_status = paid`, `paid_at` is set.

Driven route: `route` is the GPS path the driver uploaded after the trip
(`[{ lat, lng, recorded_at }]` in time order), or `null` if none was uploaded.
Only this detail endpoint returns it — lists carry `has_route` / `route_distance_km`.
`?simplify=true` drops near-collinear points (~10 m tolerance) for small maps.

parameters.name: simplify
parameters.description: Return a thinned route (fewer points, same shape)

404.description: Ride not found (or belongs to a different customer)

422.description: id must be a positive integer

post.summary: Cancel a ride before the driver arrives
post.description:
Customer can cancel while the ride is still **`requested` (1)** or **`accepted` (2)**.
Once the driver has **arrived** (3) or later, cancel is blocked (`409`).

Sets `status_id = 6` (`cancelled`), `cancelled_at`, and optional `cancellation_reason`.
If a driver was already assigned, they receive a `ride_cancelled` notification.

409.description: Ride already arrived / in progress / completed / cancelled

Driver-only. Sets how far (in km) the driver is willing to accept nearby
ride requests. New drivers default to **1 km**.

Allowed range: `0.1` – `100` km.

Driver-only. Saves the app language (`ar` or `en`). Every push and in-app
notification is sent to this driver in that language (new drivers default to `ar`).
Call it after login and whenever the driver switches language in the app.

422.description: language must be one of ar, en

get.description:
Driver-only. Returns the authenticated driver's registered vehicle
(brand, model, color, plate, type, photo, …).

get.description:
Driver-only. Returns current `wallet_balance` and transaction history
(topup, penalty, commission_deduction, compensation, reward).

get.summary: Monthly financial status
get.description:
Driver-only. Returns the authenticated driver's financial summary for a month:
- completed orders count
- total order amount (what customers paid)
- driver earnings (after commission)
- manager / platform commission from those orders
- rewards (مكافآت) and fines (غرامات) totals

Example: order `price` = 1000 with 10% commission →
`driver_earnings` = 900, `manager_earnings` = 100.

Defaults to the current year/month when query params are omitted.

post.summary: Ask to delete my account (reviewed by a manager)
post.description:
Driver-only, confirmed with the password. Creates a **pending** request — show
"Your request is under review". A manager then approves it (the account is deleted and
every device is signed out) or rejects it (the driver gets a notification with the note).

If a request is already pending, that one is returned with **200** (safe to retry).
While pending the driver can keep working and can cancel it with `DELETE`.

200.description: A request was already pending — returned as is

example.message: Your account deletion request was sent and is under review

get.summary: My latest deletion request (to show its status)
get.description:
Driver-only. Returns the most recent request (`pending`, `rejected` with `review_note`,
or `cancelled`), or `request: null` if the driver never asked.

get.summary: Am I blocked from rides? + my cancel strikes
get.description:
Driver-only. Call on app start / resume and after a `driver_blocked` or
`account_unblocked` push. While `is_blocked` the driver gets no ride offers and accept
returns 403 — show "Blocked until `blocked_until`".

`cancel_strikes` counts cancels after accept since the last manager review; at
`strike_limit` the manager is alerted and may block the account.

post.summary: Register a new driver (with personal + car images)
post.description:
`multipart/form-data` signup. Creates a driver (`status_id = 1` pending) **and**
their single vehicle in one transaction.

Images are saved on the **host** under `./uploads/` (Docker bind-mount), not inside
the container filesystem:
- personal photo → `uploads/drivers/...` → URL `/uploads/drivers/<file>`
- car photo → `uploads/vehicles/...` → URL `/uploads/vehicles/<file>`

Max image size: **5 MB**. Allowed types: JPEG, PNG, WebP.

**Form fields**
| Field | Type | Rules |
|-------|------|-------|
| `first_name` / `last_name` | text | Required, letters only |
| `phone_number` | text | Required, unique among drivers |
| `password` | text | 8–64 chars, ≥1 letter + ≥1 number |
| `address` | text | Optional |
| `device_info` | text | Optional |
| `vehicle_type_id` | text/number | Required, active vehicle type |
| `brand` / `model` / `color` | text | Required |
| `plate_number` | text | Required, unique |
| `photo` | file | **Required** personal image |
| `vehicle_photo` | file | **Required** car image |

post.summary: Log in an existing driver
post.description:
Authenticates by phone + password and issues new tokens.
**Only drivers with `status_id = 2` (active) can log in.**
Pending / suspended / rejected accounts receive **403**.

Response includes the driver profile and their vehicle (if registered).

Optional `fcm_token` (+ `platform`) is stored for Firebase push.
**Not collected on driver signup** — only on login.

403.description: Driver account is not active (pending / suspended / rejected)

errors.status_id: current status is pending; must be active
current status is suspended; must be active

post.summary: Log out the current driver session
post.description:
Soft-revokes refresh token(s). Same rules as customer logout:
- `{ "refresh_token": "..." }` → revoke this device
- `{ "all_devices": true }` → revoke all sessions

401.description: Missing/invalid access token, or refresh token invalid/already revoked

403.description: Token is not a driver token

post.summary: Request account deletion with phone + password (public web page)
post.description:
No token needed — used by the public page `GET /driver/delete-account`
(the "delete account" URL for Google Play). Works for any driver status, including
pending / suspended drivers who can't log in to the app.

Creates a **pending** request that a manager approves or rejects
(same as `POST /api/driver/account/deletion-request`). If one is already pending,
that one is returned with **200**.

- Wrong phone or wrong password → the same **401** (does not reveal who has an account).
- Limited to 5 attempts per phone and 20 per IP every 15 minutes (**429**).

200.description: A request was already pending — returned as is

401.description: Phone number or password is incorrect

get.summary: List my notifications (driver)
get.description:
Driver-only. The authenticated driver's own notifications (new ride offers, ride
updates, wallet / commission, fines, rewards, manager broadcasts…), newest first.

Notifications are kept for **1 month** — older ones are deleted automatically.
`unread_count` is the total unread for the badge (independent of page / filter).

put.summary: Mark all my notifications as read (driver)

404.description: Not found — not yours, or older than 1 month

get.summary: The driver's current ride (accepted / arrived / in_progress), or null
get.description:
For app start / resume. While `status = arrived`, `waiting.elapsed_seconds` is the
server-measured time since the driver tapped "arrived" — start the on-screen timer from
it (no clock sync needed). Socket equivalent: `driver:active_ride` is pushed on connect.

post.summary: Accept a requested ride order
post.description:
Assigns the authenticated driver to a ride that is still **`status_id = 1` (`requested`)**.
On success → **`accepted` (2)**. Atomic compare-and-set; notifies customer.

409.description: Already taken / driver has active ride

post.summary: Mark arrived at pickup location
post.description: Transition **`accepted` (2) → `arrived` (3)**. Notifies customer.

409.description: Ride is not in accepted status

post.summary: Start the trip (driver taps "Start ride" at pickup)
post.description:
Transition **`accepted` (2) or `arrived` (3) → `in_progress` (4)**.
The driver can start straight from `accepted` — calling `/pickup` first is optional.

Sets `started_at` and updates everything in one step:
- order status → `in_progress`
- driver `live_status` → `in_progress`, customer `live_status` → `in_progress`
- socket: `customer:ride_status`, `driver:ride_status`, `manager:driver_status`,
  `manager:customer_status`
- push notification to the customer (`ride_started`)

Socket alternative: emit `driver:ride_start` `{ ride_id }` with an ack.

409.description: Ride is not in accepted or arrived status

post.summary: Finish the trip — send real distance, get the final price
post.description:
Transition **`in_progress` (4) → `completed` (5)**.

The driver sends the **distance actually driven** (`distance_km`). The server
recalculates the fare and returns the **final price** to show the driver/customer:

`final_price = base_fare + distance_km × price_per_km + stops_fee_total`

- Pricing tier = the tier of this vehicle type that covers `distance_km`
  (a gap uses the tier below; outside all tiers the first / last tier — finishing never fails).
- `commission_rate` = the commission tier covering `distance_km`
  (flat rate locked at order time when no commission tiers are configured).
- `stops_fee_total` stays as locked when the order was created.
- `price` on the ride becomes the final price; the original quote is kept in `estimated_price`.

Also: sets `completed_at`, driver → `free`, customer → `idle`, sends
`customer:ride_status` (with `final_price`) + push notification with the total.

Socket alternative: emit `driver:ride_finish` `{ ride_id, distance_km }` with an ack.

distance_km.description: Distance actually driven during the trip, in km

409.description: Ride is not in in_progress status

post.summary: Pause the trip (customer stops, e.g. for a coffee)
post.description:
Only on an `in_progress` ride that isn't paused. The status stays `in_progress`;
`pause.is_paused` becomes true and a timer starts (measured by the server).
Each pause costs `base_fee` for the first `included_minutes`, then `price_per_minute`
per started minute — rules locked now (see `GET /api/admin/pause-fee`).

Also: socket `customer:ride_pause_update` / `driver:ride_pause_update`.
Socket alternative: emit `driver:ride_pause` `{ ride_id }` with an ack.

409.description: Not in progress, or already paused

post.summary: Resume the trip after a pause
post.description:
Closes the open pause: the server computes its duration and fee and adds them to
`pause.count` / `total_seconds` / `total_fee` (`pause_fee_total`), which is added to the
final price at finish. Finishing while paused closes the pause automatically.

Also: socket `customer:ride_pause_update` / `driver:ride_pause_update` with `last_pause`.
Socket alternative: emit `driver:ride_resume` `{ ride_id }` with an ack.

409.description: Trip is not paused

put.summary: Upload the driven GPS route after the trip (idempotent)
put.description:
The driver app records `lat`, `lng`, `recorded_at` every ~5 s from Start to Finish
and uploads the list **after** finish succeeds. Separate from finish on purpose —
it never changes ride status, price, payment or wallet.

PUT = replace: retries overwrite the earlier route (one stored route per ride).

Allowed when the ride has `started_at` and is `completed` (5), or `cancelled` (6)
after it started, up to **72 h** after it ended (late retries). Otherwise `409`.

The server computes `distance_km` from the points (haversine sum). The body limit
for this endpoint is 2 MB (5,000 points ≈ 350 KB).

409.description: Ride not started / not finished yet / upload window (72 h) closed

422.description:
Validation failed — 2 to 5000 points, lat -90..90, lng -180..180,
recorded_at ISO-8601 with timezone, points in time order. The error names the first bad point.

post.summary: Customer paid — split the money between driver and manager
post.description:
The driver taps **"Payment received"** after finishing the trip (customer paid cash).

Allowed only on a **`completed` (5)** ride with `payment_status = unpaid`.
In one transaction:
- ride `payment_status` → `paid`, `paid_at` set
- the driver keeps the cash (`driver_share = driver_earning_amount`)
- the manager's commission (`manager_share = admin_commission_amount`) is deducted
  from the driver's `wallet_balance` and recorded as a `commission_deduction`
  wallet transaction linked to the ride

Can only succeed once per ride (a second call returns 409, nothing is deducted twice).
The same settlement is available to managers as `POST /api/admin/orders/{id}/mark-paid`
when the driver never confirms. `data.payment` is the `RidePayment` schema.

Also: socket `customer:ride_paid`, `driver:ride_paid` (driver's other devices),
`manager:ride_paid`, push notification to the customer and the driver.

Socket alternative: emit `driver:ride_confirm_payment` `{ ride_id }` with an ack.

409.description: Ride is not completed, or payment already confirmed

post.summary: Cancel an assigned ride
post.description:
Driver cancels a ride assigned to them.

Allowed from **`accepted` / `arrived` / `in_progress`** → **`cancelled` (6)**.
Cannot cancel `requested`, `completed`, or already `cancelled` rides.

Sets `cancelled_at` and optional `cancellation_reason`. Notifies customer.

409.description: Ride cannot be cancelled in its current status

get.summary: Get the privacy policy (public)
get.description:
No token needed (show it on the signup screen / settings). One policy for both apps.

Language: `?lang=ar|en`, else the `Accept-Language` header, else `ar`.
`content` is **Markdown** (`#` headings, `-` lists, `**bold**`, `>` note, `|` tables) —
render it with a Markdown widget (e.g. `flutter_markdown`), or open `url` in a web view.
The web page https://smart-taxi.ma-core.net/privacy-policy shows the same text.

get.summary: Get the privacy policy in both languages (manager)

422.description: No content sent or text too long

get.summary: Get terms and conditions (public)
get.description:
No token needed, so it can be shown on the signup screen.
`audience` = which app: `customer` or `driver`.

Language: `?lang=ar|en`, else the `Accept-Language` header, else `ar`.
`content` is stored exactly as the manager wrote it (line breaks kept); it is
an empty string with `updated_at: null` until a manager sets it.

get.summary: Get terms and conditions in both languages (manager)

put.description:
Replaces the text for the languages sent. Send `content_ar`, `content_en`, or both
(at least one). Line breaks and spacing are kept; max 100,000 characters each.
Sending an empty string clears that language.

example.content_ar:
1. باستخدامك التطبيق فإنك توافق على هذه الشروط.
2. ...
example.content_en:
1. By using the app you agree to these terms.
2. ...

422.description: Invalid audience, no content sent, or text too long
